name: MCC Electronics
old_description: Proudly serving customers in Kansas City and around the world since 1972
about:
Mid-Continent Custom Electronics (MCCE), operating as MCC Electronics, is headquartered in Lee's Summit, Missouri, in the Kansas City metropolitan area. The company was founded in 1972 and has served customers globally from its domestic base for over five decades. In 2012, Mark Dohnalek acquired Pivot International, the global design, engineering, and manufacturing firm that owns MCCE as a subsidiary. Pivot International maintains offices in the United Kingdom and Hong Kong, with additional manufacturing plants in Kansas City and Asia, giving MCCE access to global resources while retaining U.S. production.

MCCE provides single-source original design manufacturing (ODM) and electronic manufacturing services (EMS) for electronic and electro-mechanical products. Its capabilities span hardware design, circuit board layout and assembly (both surface-mount and through-hole), embedded software development, mechanical engineering, and industrial design. The domestic facility handles prototyping, low-volume runs, and high-volume production, performing electro-mechanical panel and box assembly, device programming, custom silkscreening, encapsulating, conformal coating, and in-house test fixture construction. All products undergo 100% inspection at the U.S. plant.

The company serves a diverse industrial base, including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), agricultural equipment such as combines and hay balers, construction machinery like boom lifts, fire and emergency vehicle door systems, airport and corporate intercom control panels, hospital and detention center security systems, livestock and veterinary scales, and isokinetic exercise data logging. Customers range from OEMs needing full product development to those requiring contract assembly or design rescue.

MCCE emphasizes its domestic manufacturing oversight, global supply chain reach through Pivot International, and award-winning design team as key differentiators. The firm positions itself as a partner that can take a concept through to production, reduce costs on legacy products, improve quality, and recover troubled projects.
